title: Zechariah 1:18–21
context: Versification: English 1:18–21 is Hebrew 2:1–4, and English 2:1–13 is Hebrew 2:5–17; this page keeps the WEB numbers. In the second night vision the prophet sees four horns, which the interpreting angel explains as the powers that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem (1:18–19). The LORD then shows him four craftsmen who come to terrify and cast down those horns (1:20–21). Horns are a common biblical image of strength. Readers take the number four as standing for completeness, for the four directions, or for particular empires, and they identify the craftsmen in different ways; these notes leave those identifications open. Shared ground: both traditions read the vision as assurance that the powers which scattered God’s people are themselves under the LORD’s judgment.

verses.text: I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, four horns.
verses.arminianNotes: The prophet lifts his eyes and sees four horns. Arminian readers note that horns commonly symbolize strength or power in Scripture, preparing the reader for an image of oppressive nations.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the second vision introduced simply, with the explanation to follow. Both traditions read the four horns as symbols, and they hold the number four openly, as completeness, the four directions, or particular powers.

verses.text: I asked the angel who talked with me, “What are these?” He answered me, “These are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
verses.arminianNotes: The interpreting angel explains that these are the horns which scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem. Arminian readers see the powers that caused the exile named as responsible for their actions.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the verse identifying the instruments of past judgment, now themselves under God’s scrutiny. Shared ground: both traditions read the horns as hostile powers, without fixing them to a single list of empires.

verses.text: The LORD showed me four craftsmen.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD shows Zechariah four craftsmen. Arminian readers see craftsmen as skilled workers, perhaps those who reshape or break down, sent to answer the horns.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the craftsmen as God’s agents raised to bring down oppressors. Both traditions read the image as hopeful, and they leave the precise identification of the craftsmen open.

verses.text: Then I asked, “What are these coming to do?” He said, “These are the horns which scattered Judah, so that no man lifted up his head; but these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.”
verses.arminianNotes: The craftsmen come to terrify and cast down the horns that scattered Judah so that no one could lift his head. Arminian readers see God’s justice reversing oppression and lifting up his people.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s sovereignty over the nations, raising up one power to judge another. Shared ground: both traditions read the vision as assurance that no oppressor is beyond the LORD’s reach.
